title: Scalar normalization of the chart left comparison
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On either the ordinary etale or pro-etale site let $\mathcal C_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T,R)$ mean the full category of constant-$R$ module complexes with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: tensor with any degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer]. Write $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The finite Tate line is $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ on the etale site and its comparison inverse image on the pro-etale site; $(d)$ denotes tensor with its $d$th tensor power [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].
Let $e:U\to V=\mathbf A^d_Y$ be separated etale of finite type, put $g=p_de$, and choose compactifications of $e,p_d,g$ with middle schemes in the standing setting [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the ordinary etale site write $E_R=De_{\Sigma!,R}$ for exact sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], $F_{d,R}=Rp_{d!,R}$ and $F_{g,R}=Rg_{!,R}$ for the chosen compact-support candidates [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Let $c_{e,R}:F_{e,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_R$ be the graph-normalized comparison, let $\alpha_R:F_{d,R}F_{e,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g,R}$ be canonical composition with the chosen common-refinement identifications, and put $\lambda_R=\alpha_R\circ F_{d,R}(c_{e,R}^{-1}):F_{d,R}E_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g,R}$ [def-sp-etale-adjoint-chart-comparison, def-sp-etale-compact-support-normalization]. Let $\sigma_e:T_VE_A\xrightarrow{\sim}E_BT_U$ be summandwise tensor and let $\beta_d,\beta_g$ be the proper-counit/open-tensor coefficient maps [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. On $\mathcal C_{U,A}$, $\lambda_R$ is an isomorphism and
$$\beta_g\circ T_Y(\lambda_A)=\lambda_BT_U\circ F_{d,B}(\sigma_e)\circ\beta_d E_A.$$
The comparison $\lambda_R$ carries the composite of the affine-space adjunction and $E_R\dashv e_R^*$ to the adjunction for $F_{g,R}$, retaining its sum-then-affine counit. The equation holds for every specified compactification via its canonical common-refinement comparison. No flatness of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Charts: counit-preserving left identification and its coefficient square; retained Step 11, last five sentences

proof.text: Work on the ordinary etale site, as in the asserted equation. By [lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain], each $F_{h,R}$ and coefficient extension preserves the indicated finite-Tor categories. By [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization], $c_{e,R}:F_{e,R}\simeq E_R$ is the canonical refinement-compatible isomorphism, so $E_R$ also preserves this category. The composition comparison $\alpha_R$ is an isomorphism by [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Hence $\lambda_R=\alpha_RF_{d,R}(c_{e,R}^{-1})$ is an isomorphism. Take the datum of [def-sp-etale-compact-support-normalization] entering [def-sp-etale-adjoint-chart-comparison] to be the family $c_{v,c}$ of [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]: its degree-zero sum-component description gives the graph-extension condition and the derived formula for $c^{-1}$, and its proper-refinement agreement, base-change square with identity and composition normalization, and counit identification are the remaining conditions of the datum. So the comparison $c_e$ used here is the one that enters [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] in Steps 3–5. The specified chart comparison of [def-sp-etale-adjoint-chart-comparison] uses a compatible restricted-closure compactification; refinement compatibility of $c_e$ and composition identifies it with this same formula for the independently chosen compactifications.

source.place: Charts: normalized chart left comparison and coefficient compatibility

proof.text: Write $G_{d,R}=p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$, $H_R=e_R^*G_{d,R}$, and let $v_R:E_Re_R^*\to\mathrm{id}$ be the sum/evaluation counit. The affine adjunction is the ordered one of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], and the sum adjunction is specified by [def-sp-etale-adjoint-chart-comparison]. By the explicit composite-adjunction formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], the counit for $L_R=F_{d,R}E_R\dashv H_R$ is $\delta_{R,K}=\epsilon_{d,R,K}\circ F_{d,R}(v_{R,G_{d,R}K})$. Transfer its Hom bijection to $F_{g,R}$ by sending $a:F_{g,R}M\to K$ first to $a\circ\lambda_{R,M}:L_RM\to K$, then to its composite adjunct. Precomposition with $\lambda_R$ is a natural bijection, with inverse precomposition with $\lambda_R^{-1}$. Evaluating the resulting Hom bijection at the identity of $H_RK$ gives the counit $\epsilon_{g,R,K}=\delta_{R,K}\circ\lambda_{R,H_RK}^{-1}$, so $\epsilon_{g,R,K}\circ\lambda_{R,H_RK}=\delta_{R,K}$. This is precisely the chart adjunction obtained using the specified left comparison. It retains the actual sum-then-affine counit, rather than choosing a new trace.

source.place: Charts: normalized chart left comparison and coefficient compatibility

proof.text:
For $M\in\mathcal C_{U,A}$, [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] gives $c_{e,B,T_UM}\circ\beta_{e,M}=\sigma_{e,M}\circ T_V(c_{e,A,M})$. Compose on the left with $c_{e,B,T_UM}^{-1}$ and on the right with $T_V(c_{e,A,M}^{-1})$. Functoriality and cancellation yield
$$\beta_{e,M}\circ T_V(c_{e,A,M}^{-1})=c_{e,B,T_UM}^{-1}\circ\sigma_{e,M}.$$
This uses the stated graph-normalized comparison, not an arbitrary isomorphism from $F_e$ to sum extension.

source.place: Charts: normalized chart left comparison and coefficient compatibility

proof.text:
Apply the composition equation of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] to $(e,p_d)$, and then naturality of $\beta_d$ at $c_{e,A,M}^{-1}:E_AM\to F_{e,A}M$. Suppressing only component subscripts, the resulting calculation is
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_gT_Y(\lambda_A)
&=\alpha_BT_U\,F_{d,B}(\beta_e)\,\beta_dF_{e,A}\,T_YF_{d,A}(c_{e,A}^{-1})\\
&=\alpha_BT_U\,F_{d,B}\bigl(\beta_e\circ T_V(c_{e,A}^{-1})\bigr)\,\beta_dE_A\\
&=\alpha_BT_U\,F_{d,B}(c_{e,B}^{-1}T_U)\,F_{d,B}(\sigma_e)\,\beta_dE_A\\
&=\lambda_BT_U\,F_{d,B}(\sigma_e)\,\beta_dE_A.
\end{aligned}$$
The third line is Step 3. Every arrow is $B$-linear with source $T_YF_{d,A}E_A$ and target $F_{g,B}T_U$; in particular no inverse of $\beta_d$ and no flatness of $B$ over $A$ has been used.

source.place: Charts: normalized chart left comparison and coefficient compatibility

proof.text: For another specified compactification of $g$, write $\rho_R:F_{g,R}\simeq F'_{g,R}$ for the canonical common-refinement comparison. Coherence of composition in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] gives $\lambda'_R=\rho_R\lambda_R$. The refinement square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] says $\beta'_gT_Y(\rho_A)=\rho_BT_U\,\beta_g$. Thus the left side of Step 4 for $\lambda'$ is $\rho_BT_U$ times its old left side, and its right side is $\rho_BT_U$ times its old right side. For a change of the compactification of $e$, refinement compatibility in [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] gives $c'_e\rho_e=c_e$, so $\rho_e$ cancels in $\alpha'F_d((c'_e)^{-1})$. For a change of the compactification of $p_d$, naturality and coherent composition give $\lambda'_R\circ(\rho_{d,R}E_R)=\lambda_R$; its coefficient square is the same refinement square, now for $p_d$, whiskered by $E_A$. These identities prove the equation for every set of choices. The transported counit formula in Step 2 likewise becomes $\epsilon'_g=\epsilon_g\rho_H^{-1}$ under a change of $g$; substituting $\lambda'=\rho\lambda$ cancels $\rho_H^{-1}\rho_H$. Changes of the two constituent models are already the adjunction-preserving identifications used to define the ordered affine adjunction and the graph-normalized sum comparison. Common-refinement independence and the cocycle law make these identifications independent of the refinement chosen.
